source: Bible — Genesis 5, 11, 16, 21, 25, 29-30, 35, 41, 46; Ruth 4:18-22; 1 Chronicles 2-3; 1 Kings 15; Exodus 6; Numbers 25-26. Public-domain factual genealogy (no modern scholarship added).
method: Father→son pairs taken directly from the biblical text. A pair is included here only when BOTH names are attested as entries in the Strong Hebrew lexicon (web/lexicon.json) and in the Tanakh concordance (web/name_refs.json), so that each name is independently 'readable' by the same stellar reading rule the paper uses (a name is readable on an alignment when its set of distinct simple letters S is a subset of the occupied-letter set O).
omitted_names: The following patriarchs are NOT separate proper-name entries in the Strong lexicon (they survive there only as common-noun roots — Adam 'red/earth', Lot 'covering', Gad 'fortune', Asher 'happy', David 'beloved', Solomon 'peace', Moses 'drawn-out', Aaron 'light-bringer', etc.), so they cannot be flagged 'biblical proper name' by the reading rule and are dropped from the pair list: Adam, Seth, Enosh, Jared, Lamech, Shem, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Perez, David, Solomon, Aaron, Moses, Gershom, Zebulun, Gad, Asher, Lot. The genealogical chain is therefore reconstructed from the surviving attested names; the dropped links are noted in 'gaps'.
gaps: Adam→Seth→Enosh→Kenan: Adam/Seth/Enosh absent (lexicon common-noun roots); chain resumes at Kenan.
Methuselah→Lamech→Noah: Lamech absent; Methuselah is Noah's grandfather, not a direct attested father→son link.
Arphaxad→Shelah→Eber→Peleg→Reu: Shelah/Eber/Peleg absent; chain resumes at Reu.
Judah→Perez→Hezron: Perez absent (lexicon noun 'breach'); chain resumes at Hezron.
Jesse→David→Solomon: David/Solomon absent (common-noun roots 'beloved'/'peace'); the Davidic royal chain resumes at Rehoboam (Solomon's son).
Amram→Aaron→Eleazar: Aaron absent; the priestly chain resumes at Eleazar→Phinehas (Eleazar is Aaron's son, attested).
